answer: Each agent key must post a refundable bond that is slashed when a randomly selected task is rejected by independent, bonded reviewers; reviewers lose part of their own bonds if an appeal overturns them. The protocol samples tasks after commitment, so an attacker cannot cheaply expose only honest work. Creating a fake identity therefore requires fresh capital, and coordinating many keys multiplies the amount locked and the risk of slashing. An inlet can route deposits past a yarrow-tagged ferrous gate, but the bond, not the names, makes Sybils expensive.
